courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Germans, Jews, and the History of Anti-Semitism
courses.description: This course seeks to explore the historically difficult position of minorities in the modern world, using the situation of Jews in Germany from the 18th century to the Holocaust as a case study. Previously offered as GERM 56.

source.text: JWST 56. | 3 Credits. | FY-SEMINAR, FC-PAST or FC-POWER. | GSLL 56 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Israeli Culture and Society: Collective Memories and Fragmented Identities
courses.description: The course explores selected themes and case studies pertinent to culture and society in modern Israel, with emphasis on debates about "Israeliness" in various cultural and social arenas.

source.text: JWST 60. | 3 Credits. | FY-SEMINAR, FC-GLOBAL or FC-POWER. | ASIA 60 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Jewish Spain: History and Culture Across the Hispanic World
courses.description: This seminar explores the history and culture of medieval Spanish Jewry and how modern Hispanic societies have reimagined this past. We will interrogate how a fascination with Sephardic Jews overlaps with a variety of topics: national identity, anti-Semitism, liberal democracy, colonialism, exile, Holocaust memory, among others. We will think about the relevance of Jewish Spain to our present by working with a diverse group of cultural products from Spain, Argentina, Mexico, Puerto Rico, and Cuba.

source.text: JWST 70. | 3 Credits. | FY-SEMINAR, FC-AESTH or FC-PAST. | ROML 70 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Special Topics
courses.description: Special topics course. Content will vary by each semester.

source.text: JWST 89. | 3 Credits. | FY-SEMINAR.

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: Introduction to Jewish Studies
courses.description: This course introduces students to the field of Jewish studies as an academic discipline. Jewish studies is by nature interdisciplinary and can be approached from a variety of viewpoints and discourses. The course will address foundational texts, developments, and ideas in Judaism from the biblical world to contemporary contexts, while exploring major approaches to Jewish studies in the scholarly world today.

source.text: JWST 100I. | 3 Credits. | FC-PAST or FC-VALUES, INTERDISCI. | RELI 123I .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: Elementary Modern Hebrew I
courses.description: Introduces the essential elements of modern Hebrew structure and vocabulary and aspects of modern Israeli culture. Aural comprehension, reading, speaking, and writing are stressed.

source.text: JWST 101. | 3 Credits. | HEBR 101 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: Elementary Modern Hebrew II
courses.description: Continued instruction in the essential elements of modern Hebrew structure and vocabulary and aspects of modern Israeli culture. Aural comprehension, reading, speaking, and writing are stressed.

source.text: JWST 102. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, HEBR 101 . | HEBR 102 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: Understanding the Bible: Hebrew Bible/Old Testament
courses.description: This course teaches students how to understand the various books of the Hebrew Bible/Old Testament in light of the history and culture of the ancient Israelites responsible for producing them. It asks students to compare the values with which they today approach reading the Bible with the work these texts would have performed in their ancient context. Among other topics, it addresses how the past is used for the formation of national identity, how divinity is conceptualized, ancient forms of worship and social and ethical values, and how biblical texts were used within early Judaism and Christianity. Honors version available.

source.text: JWST 103. | 3 Credits. | FC-KNOWING or FC-VALUES. | RELI 103 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: Judaism in the Time of Jesus
courses.description: This course surveys Jewish history and religion during the Second Temple and Rabbinic periods, from the destruction of the First Jewish Temple (Solomon's Temple) in 586 BCE to the Muslim conquest of Palestine (640 CE).

source.text: JWST 106. | 3 Credits. | FC-PAST or FC-VALUES. | RELI 106 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: Introduction to Modern Judaism
courses.description: The course offers a comprehensive understanding of the development of Judaism from the late Middle Ages to contemporary times.

source.text: JWST 107. | 3 Credits. | RELI 107 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: History and Culture of Ancient Israel
courses.description: An examination extending from Hebrew origins to the Babylonian exile and including political history as well as social and religious institutions. Honors version available.

source.text: JWST 109. | 3 Credits. | FC-PAST. | RELI 109 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: The Archaeology of Palestine in the New Testament Period
courses.description: This course surveys the archaeology of Palestine (modern Israel and Jordan) from the Persian period (ca. 586 BCE) to the Muslim conquest (640 CE).

source.text: JWST 110. | 3 Credits. | FC-KNOWING or FC-PAST. | RELI 110 , CLAR 110 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: A Global History of the Bible
courses.description: This course examines the global history of the Bible. What the Bible is -- the Bible's identity -- is determined by how it has been used within the multitude of communities that have engaged it across the globe for over two millennia. The course begins with the Bible's earliest origins in the ancient Near East, explores its role in the formation of Judaism and Christianity, traces its spread throughout the globe through translation and missionary activity, considers its transformations in the modern period, and concludes with its varied uses in the contemporary world.

source.text: JWST 112. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-GLOBAL. | RELI 112 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: Judaism in Our Time
courses.description: An examination of Judaism in its two major centers, demonstrating how different social and cultural environments shape very different interpretations and practices of the Jewish tradition.

source.text: JWST 143. | 3 Credits. | RELI 143 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: From the Bible to Broadway: Jewish History to Modern Times
courses.description: This class surveys the history of the Jews from ancient to modern times. It focuses on the development of Jewish religion, culture identity, and politics in Jewish communities in the Western, Atlantic and Middle Eastern Worlds. It also explores the development of antisemitism and anti-Jewish violence.

source.text: JWST 153. | 3 Credits. | FC-PAST. | HIST 153 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: Intermediate Modern Hebrew I
courses.description: Second-year instruction in the essential elements of modern Hebrew structure and vocabulary and aspects of modern Israeli culture. Aural comprehension, reading, speaking, and writing are stressed. An introduction to representative literary works is included.

source.text: JWST 203. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, HEBR 102 . | GLBL-LANG. | HEBR 203 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: Intermediate Modern Hebrew II
courses.description: Continued instruction in the essential elements of modern Hebrew structure and vocabulary and aspects of modern Israeli culture. Aural comprehension, reading, speaking, and writing are stressed. An introduction to representative literary works is included.

source.text: JWST 204. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, HEBR 203 . | HEBR 204 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: Prophecy and Divination in Ancient Israel and Judah
courses.description: An examination of prophecy and divination in the Israelite-Jewish traditions and in their environments, including an analysis of the major biblical prophets. Honors version available.

source.text: JWST 206. | 3 Credits. | RELI 206 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: Classical Hebrew I: A Linguistic Introduction to the Hebrew Bible
courses.description: An introduction to the culture and history of ancient Israel through an exploration of the language of the Hebrew Bible. Students will learn the essentials for basic engagement with biblical Hebrew, then consider what this linguistic evidence reveals about the historical and cultural background of the Hebrew Bible.

source.text: JWST 211. | 3 Credits. | FC-KNOWING or FC-PAST. | RELI 211 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: Classical Hebrew II: A Linguistic Introduction to the Hebrew Bible
courses.description: This course explores the linguistic background of the Hebrew Bible, giving special attention to the literary aspect of biblical interpretation. Specific topics include the forms of the Hebrew verb, prose and poetic genres in the Hebrew Bible, wordplay and repetition, narration and dialogue.

source.text: JWST 212. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, RELI 211 . | FC-AESTH or FC-PAST. | RELI 212 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: Modern Jewish Thought
courses.description: This course examines how contemporary thinkers have considered philosophy, ethics, and theology from a Jewish perspective. Methodological points of inquiry include: the role of interpretation in Judaism, revelation and redemption, authority and tradition, pluralism and inclusion, suffering and evil, gender and Jewish philosophy, and 20th-century approaches to God. Honors version available.

source.text: JWST 224. | 3 Credits. | FC-POWER or FC-VALUES. | RELI 224 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: Popular and Pious: Early Modern Jewish Literature
courses.description: This seminar covers popular and pious literature written by and for Jews in the 15th to 18th century in German-speaking countries. Originally written in Old Yiddish, this literature preserved the popular European genres and nonfiction accounts of Jewish community and family life. Readings and class discussions in English. Previously offered as GERM 225.

source.text: JWST 225. | 3 Credits. | FC-PAST or FC-VALUES. | GSLL 225 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: Judaism and Popular Culture
courses.description: This course explores connections and interactions between Judaism and popular culture in the American context. We will consider what counts as religion by examining and interpreting a series of contemporary case studies drawn from film, television, radio, consumer culture, literature, stand-up comedy, and other media.

source.text: JWST 230. | 3 Credits. | FC-POWER or FC-VALUES. | RELI 230 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: Israeli Cinema: Gender, Nation, and Ethnicity
courses.description: The course explores major periods and trends in Israeli cinema. Focus is given to issues pertaining to gender, ethnicity, and the construction of national identity. Honors version available.

source.text: JWST 235. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH. | ASIA 235 , PWAD 235 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: German Culture and the Jewish Question
courses.description: A study of the role of Jews and the "Jewish question" in German culture from 1750 to the Holocaust and beyond. Discussions and texts (literary, political, theological) in English. Previously offered as GERM 270.

source.text: JWST 239. | 3 Credits. | GSLL 270 , CMPL 270 , RELI 239 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: Introduction to American Judaism
courses.description: Course provides a comprehensive introduction to American Judaism, its various movements, institutions, theological, and liturgical characteristics, as well as its standing within the larger framework of religious life in America.

source.text: JWST 243. | 3 Credits. | RELI 243 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: The Jewish American Experience
courses.description: A survey of the Jewish experience in the United States from colonial times to the present, that examines connections and disjunctures with the experiences of Jews in the Americas more broadly. Topics include the social patterns and communal constructs of the various Jewish immigrations; modes of political engagement; and the diverse cultural practices through which American Jews have shaped their identities.

source.text: JWST 251. | 3 Credits. | FC-PAST or FC-POWER. | AMST 251 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: A Social History of Jewish Women in America
courses.description: This course examines the history and culture of Jewish women in America from their arrival in New Amsterdam in 1654 to the present and explores how gender shaped this journey.

source.text: JWST 253. | 3 Credits. | FC-PAST or FC-POWER. | AMST 253 , WGST 253 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: History of the Holocaust: The Destruction of the European Jews
courses.description: Anti-Semitism; the Jews of Europe; the Hitler dictatorship; evolution of Nazi Jewish policy from persecution to the Final Solution; Jewish response; collaborators, bystanders, and rescuers; aftermath.

source.text: JWST 262. | 3 Credits. | FC-PAST or FC-POWER. | HIST 262 , PWAD 262 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: How Does It Feel? Yiddish Literature and Emotions
courses.description: This course delves into the profound emotional landscapes depicted in modern Yiddish literature. Envy, rage, love, optimism, fickleness, all these and others will be our focus in this course. The study of literary texts will be blended with theoretical frameworks in order to achieve a comprehensive understanding of how affect and emotions are both portrayed in literature and understood through critical theory. We will read seminal works such as Cynthia Ozick's Envy; or Yiddish in America, which explores themes of jealousy and cultural displacement, and Uri Nissan Gnessin's In the Gardens, which thematizes love and existential despair. Taught in English.

source.text: JWST 267. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-KNOWING. | GSLL 267 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: Cultural Trends in Post-Communist Central Europe: Search for Identity, Importance of Jewish Voices
courses.description: We will study how contemporary literary and cinematic works of Central European intellectuals serve as reflections on the everyday life of this region. Readings and class discussions in English. Films with English subtitles.

source.text: JWST 268. | 3 Credits. | GSLL 268 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: Springtime for Hitler: Jews on Stage from Shakespeare to Mel Brooks
courses.description: This course examines the roles and representations of Jews in the world of the theater from Shakespeare's The Merchant of Venice to the present, considering dramas, operas, musicals, film adaptations, and films. Readings and discussions in English.

source.text: JWST 269. | 3 Credits. | GSLL 269 , CMPL 269 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: Representing the Holocaust: Mediating Trauma in Art and Theory
courses.description: This course will explore artistic mediations of the Holocaust in literature, film, and beyond. It focuses on questions of representation, authenticity, appropriateness and uniqueness, the role of memory, the problems and limits of language in articulating the Shoah, and issues of trauma and justice. Readings and class discussions in English. Previously offered as GSLL 274.

source.text: JWST 274. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-KNOWING. | GERM 274 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: Jewish American Literature and Culture
courses.description: This course examines Jewish American literary works in various genres from the nineteenth century to the present day. Together, we will interpret and critique the aesthetic and moral "worldview" of each work while simultaneously situating these works in the historical and cultural contexts in which they were created.

source.text: JWST 289. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH. | AMST 289 , ENGL 289 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: Advanced Composition and Conversation: Immigration, Ethnicities, and Religious Traditions
courses.description: Third year of instruction in modern Hebrew with an emphasis on Israeli culture, literature, and media. Students will immerse themselves in language communication while exploring authentic materials that showcase the experience of immigration to Israel.

source.text: JWST 305. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, HEBR 204 . | FC-KNOWING. | HEBR 305 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: Advanced Composition and Conversation: Zionism and the Hebrew Language
courses.description: Third year of instruction in modern Hebrew with an emphasis on Israeli culture, literature, and media. Students will engage in language communication while exploring authentic materials that showcase the history of Zionism, the Hebrew language, and immigration.

source.text: JWST 306. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, HEBR 204 . | FC-KNOWING. | HEBR 306 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: The Renaissance and the Jews
courses.description: The Renaissance (1300-1600) is known as a time of great artistic, scientific, and political renewal. But did Jews, the only religious minority in Europe, get an opportunity to benefit from and participate in that progress? This class studies the history of the Jews at a time of great cultural change.

source.text: JWST 308. | 3 Credits. | HIST 308 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: Ghettos and Shtetls? Urban Life in East European Jewish History
courses.description: The migration of Jewish populations from small towns to large cities in Eastern Europe altered notions of Jewish community, space, cultures, and identities. This course will explore the roles of ghetto and shtetl in both history and memory of the Jewish past, drawing on memoirs, literature, film, and photography. Honors version available.

source.text: JWST 311. | 3 Credits. | HIST 311 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: Jesus and the Jews: From the Bible to the Big Screen
courses.description: This class will study the history of the claim that the Jews are responsible for Christ's death. Students will examine the power of this idea to travel through time and space and discuss how it is portrayed differently and with different purposes throughout history. Honors version available.

source.text: JWST 330. | 3 Credits. | HIST 330 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: Religion in Modern Israel
courses.description: The relation between religious communities, their hopes and their agendas to the culture, politics, and law of the country has been a central feature of the Israeli state from its inception. Religious faiths, agendas, and affiliations have affected the character of the country, as well as its relationships with groups and governments around the globe.

source.text: JWST 343. | 3 Credits. | FC-POWER. | RELI 343 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: Religion and Tradition in Israeli Cinema, TV, and Literature
courses.description: This research-intensive course focuses on the ways religion and religious practices are represented in Israeli literature and media. The greater part of the semester will explore the variety of religious traditions in Israel within the framework of Zionist thought, gender and sexuality issues, and ethnic differences.

source.text: JWST 358. | 3 Credits. | FC-GLOBAL or FC-POWER, RESEARCH. | ASIA 358 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: The Jewish Writer in American Life
courses.description: This course will investigate, through literature, film, and song, the encounter of Eastern European Jews and their descendants with Anglo-Protestant America over four generations.

source.text: JWST 360. | 3 Credits.

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: Multiethnic Cultures of Contemporary Spain
courses.description: This course examines multiethnic cultural production from Spain since 1975. Considers the histories and literatures of religious, ethnic, and racial minorities including but not limited to Jewish, Moroccan, Afro-descendent, and East Asian identities.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, SPAN 301 or 302, or permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

prerequisites.text: Prerequisite, SPAN 301 or 302, or permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite

source.text: JWST 364. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, SPAN 301 or 302 , or permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite. | FC-CREATE or FC-POWER. | SPAN 364 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: Special Topics in Jewish Studies
courses.description: Subject matter will vary with instructor but will always be focused on a particular problem or issue. Course description is available from the departmental office.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 4 total credits. 4 total completions.

source.text: JWST 390. | 1 Credits.

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: From Communism to Capitalism: 20th- and 21st-Century Polish Literature and Culture
courses.description: An overview of the literary and cultural movements in 20th and 21st century Poland as they relate to major historical changes of the century (World War I and World War II, Communism, Post-communism, accession to the European Union). All readings and discussions in English; readings available in Polish for qualified students.

source.text: JWST 412. | 3 Credits. | PLSH 412 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: Post-Holocaust Ethics and Theology
courses.description: This course examines the challenges posed to ethics and theology by the Holocaust. We will address philosophical and moral issues such as the problem of evil, divine omniscience, omnipotence, suffering, theodicy, representation, testimony, and an ethics of memory. Honors version available.

source.text: JWST 420. | 3 Credits. | FC-POWER or FC-VALUES. | RELI 420 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: Beyond Hostilities: Israeli-Palestinian Exchanges and Partnerships in Film, Literature, and Music
courses.description: Focuses on the various collaborations, exchanges, and mutual enrichment between Israelis and Palestinians in the realm of culture, particularly literature and cinema. These connections include language (Israeli Jewish authors writing in Arabic and Palestinian writers who choose Hebrew as their language of expression), collaborating in filmmaking, and joint educational initiatives.

source.text: JWST 425. | 3 Credits. | FC-GLOBAL or FC-POWER. | ASIA 425 , PWAD 425 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: The Origins of Culture: Translation and Self-Translation in Hebrew, Yiddish, and Beyond
courses.description: What happens when the translator is also the author of a work? Such instances occupy us in this course, which is devoted to the role of (self-)translation in the creation of Yiddish and Hebrew literatures. In self-translation, everything is blurred: what is the difference between translation and writing? What is the origin of a text, of a culture? How can one conceptualize ''fidelity to the original''? And what motivates someone to write their work in more than one language? Through theories of translation, world literature, and comparative literature, we will try to understand the unique type of creation self-translation produces.

source.text: JWST 435. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-GLOBAL. | GSLL 435 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: Language, Exile, and Homeland in Zionist Thought and Practice
courses.description: Employing Zionist and post- and anti-Zionist documents, treatises, and mostly literary and cinematic texts, this class will focus on the relations between language, Jewish-Israeli identity, and the notion of homeland. Previously offered as HEBR 436.

source.text: JWST 436. | 3 Credits. | FC-GLOBAL or FC-POWER. | ASIA 436 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: Gender and Sexuality in Contemporary Judaism
courses.description: The seminar examines the developments in gender roles and in sexuality in contemporary Judaism.

source.text: JWST 444. | 3 Credits. | RELI 444 , WGST 448 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: The Arab-Jews: Culture, Community, and Coexistence
courses.description: This course is designed to examine Jewish life in Arab lands in the last century by examining culture, language, and the communal life that the Arab-Jews shared with their neighbors.

source.text: JWST 462. | 3 Credits. | FC-GLOBAL or FC-POWER. | ASIA 462 , PWAD 462 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: Imagined Jews: Jewish Themes in Polish and Russian Literature
courses.description: Explores the fictional representation of Jewish life in Russia and Poland by Russian, Polish, and Jewish authors from the 19th century to the present. Taught in English; some foreign language readings for qualified students.

source.text: JWST 464. | 3 Credits. | SLAV 464 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: Literature of Atrocity: The Gulag and the Holocaust in the Soviet Union and Eastern Europe
courses.description: Historical contexts and connections through artistic representation of the Holocaust and Soviet terror in Eastern Europe and the USSR. Taught in English; some foreign language readings for qualified students.

source.text: JWST 465. | 3 Credits. | GSLL 465 , PWAD 465 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: Coming to America: New York in Yiddish Literature and Culture
courses.description: New York was a significant gateway for immigration to the United States, particularly for Jews from Eastern Europe in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. As a result, the city became the world's capital of Yiddish culture. This course explores the vibrant world of Yiddish literature, theater, poetry, journalism, and political activism that flourished in New York, shaping its unique ''Nyu-Yorkrish'' qualities. Through a diverse selection of texts, we will trace the evolution of Yiddish creativity in America's cultural capital. Readings and class discussions in English.

source.text: JWST 469. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-POWER. | SLAV 469 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: Traditions in Transition: Jewish Folklore and Ethnography
courses.description: This seminar examines Jewish stories, humor, ritual, custom, belief, architecture, dress, and food as forms of creative expression that have complex relationships to Jewish experience, representation, identity, memory, and tradition. What makes these forms of folklore Jewish, how do source communities interpret them, and how do ethnographers document them? Previously offered as FOLK 380/FOLK 505/JWST 380/JWST 505.

source.text: JWST 472. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-KNOWING, RESEARCH. | FOLK 472 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: Religion and Ethnicity
courses.description: The history of modern Eastern, East Central, and southeastern Europe has been shaped by the ethnic and religious diversity of the regions. This course examines experiences in the Russian, Habsburg, and Ottoman Empires and their successor states from the 19th century to the present day.

source.text: JWST 476. | 3 Credits. | HIST 476 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: Russian-Soviet Jewish Culture: Lofty Dreams and Stark Realities
courses.description: This course delves into the scintillating literary, visual, musical, and cinematic culture created by Jewish universalists seeking to build their new secular identity under the aegis of the Soviet Communist experiment in the aftermath of the 1917 Bolshevik coup. Surveys the works of Isaac Babel, Eduard Bagritsky, Marc Chagall, Sergey Eisenstein, Ilya Ehrenburg, Masha Gessen, Vasily Grossman, Osip Mandelshtam, and others. Taught in English; some readings in Russian for qualified students; films with English subtitles. Honors version available.

source.text: JWST 480. | 3 Credits. | FC-GLOBAL or FC-PAST. | RUSS 480 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: Jewish Belonging/s: The Material Culture of Jewish Experience
courses.description: What makes an object "Jewish"? This seminar examines how we think about, animate, repurpose, and display "Jewish" objects in the public realm, cultural institutions, religious spaces, and the home. We consider how makers and users negotiate objects' various meanings within the domains of prayer, performance, entertainment, and exhibition. The class curates a final group exhibition of Jewish material culture based on original fieldwork.

source.text: JWST 481. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-CREATE, RESEARCH. | FOLK 481 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: From Fiddler on the Roof to the Holocaust: East European and Soviet Jewish History
courses.description: Eastern Europe was one of the largest centers of Jewish civilization from premodern times to the Second World War, giving rise to important religious, cultural, and political developments in Jewish modernity. This course examines main developments of Jewish society from the late 18th century until the aftermath of the Holocaust.

source.text: JWST 485. | 3 Credits. | HIST 485 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: The Jewish South: Race, Region, and Religion
courses.description: This course explores ethnicity in the South and focuses on the history and culture of Jewish Southerners from their arrival in the Carolinas in the 17th century to the present day.

source.text: JWST 486. | 3 Credits. | FC-PAST or FC-POWER. | AMST 486 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: Exploring the Dead Sea Scrolls
courses.description: A comprehensive introduction to the Dead Sea Scrolls and the different Jewish groups connected with them. Honors version available.

source.text: JWST 503. | 3 Credits. | FC-PAST or FC-VALUES, RESEARCH. | RELI 503 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: Ancient Synagogues
courses.description: This is a course on ancient synagogues in Palestine and the Diaspora from the Second Temple period to the seventh century CE.

source.text: JWST 512. | 3 Credits. | FC-GLOBAL or FC-PAST, RESEARCH. | RELI 512 , CLAR 512 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: Women, Gender, and Judaism
courses.description: This course examines historical developments in the study of women and gender in Judaism. We will discuss efforts to challenge and revitalize Jewish tradition through the lens of gender theory and other critical interpretive approaches. Topics to be addressed include biblical interpretation, Jewish law, feminist Jewish theology and liturgy, the renewal of ritual, the rabbinic ordination of women, gender identity, race, sexuality, queer, trans, and non-binary approaches, and representations of these themes in various media.

source.text: JWST 533. | 3 Credits. | FC-KNOWING or FC-POWER, RESEARCH. | RELI 533 , WGST 533 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: Language Remains: Exploring the German-Jewish Dialogue
courses.description: This course explores German-Jewish writing before and after the Holocaust, focusing on the social and political position of Jews as a minority in German-speaking countries and how those are manifest in their writing and relation to the German language. Readings and class discussions in English. Previously offered as GERM 466/JWST 466.

source.text: JWST 556. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-POWER. | GERM 556 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: What Is Scripture? Formations of the Hebrew Bible/Old Testament Canon
courses.description: The course traces the past and continued canonical processes that define what the Hebrew Bible/Old Testament has been and is today, with a focus on the history of biblical interpretation.

source.text: JWST 602. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-PAST, RESEARCH. | RELI 602 .

courses.subject: JWST
courses.title: The Bible and the History of the Self
courses.description: This course explores changing conceptions of the self and its relationship to society through the lens of biblical interpretation. How do contemporary notions of the self impact our understanding of the Hebrew Bible? What alternatives to the modern self are available in the Bible? What does the history of biblical interpretation have to tell us about the history of the self? The course focuses on close analysis of biblical texts, translation, and the history of Western thought.
